A1.justification: Both PDFs describe Editable Concept Bottleneck Models. Their text, equations, tables, figures, and complete appendices support comparison, including matching relocated visualizations.

before.justification: V2 reports original experiments on OAI, CUB, and CelebA, including utility, runtime, concept-importance, and membership-inference results.

after.justification: V3 retains these original experiments and adds synthetic-noise removal and periodic-editing results in Appendix H.2–H.3.

M1.justification: Algorithms 1–8 are unchanged. However, v3 Theorem 4.6 defines the label-predictor Hessian using edited concepts, whereas v2 Theorem 4.5 uses original concepts. V3's Algorithm 2 and corresponding proof retain the original definition, leaving an intended procedural change versus an equation inconsistency unresolved.

E1.justification: OAI, CUB, CelebA, and the three editing tasks remain. Appendix H.2–H.3 adds CUB evaluation under deliberately corrupted training concepts and class labels, extending input conditions without adding a dataset or domain.

E2.justification: Table 1 and Figure 2 retain the same Retrain, CBM-IF, and ECBM comparisons. The added analyses compare ECBM with the existing retraining comparator; newly cited unlearning methods are not evaluated.

E3.justification: Appendix H.2–H.3 introduces controlled 10% corruption and ten successive 1% editing rounds, with each ECBM update starting from the previously edited model. These new evaluation designs also report accuracy alongside F1. The original main-table sampling and repetition settings remain.

E4.justification: Beyond the retained editing-ratio, concept-importance, and membership-inference analyses, v3 adds harmful-data-removal and periodic-editing studies across all three editing levels. Figures 5–8 test recovery from corrupted training information and performance over repeated updates.

E5.justification: Both versions give the same five-seed and ten-repeat descriptions and identical F1 uncertainty entries in Table 1. The new appendix experiments introduce no reported uncertainty-estimation or significance-testing procedure.

E6.justification: All 27 Table 1 runtimes are replaced, while F1 values and their uncertainty entries remain identical. For OAI concept-label editing, Retrain/ECBM changes from 31.44/8.29 seconds to 297.77/2.36 minutes, which is not a unit conversion; the measurement relationship is unexplained. Figures 5–8 additionally report utility recovery and repeated-edit performance.

T1.justification: V3 adds quantitative concept-predictor approximation bounds in Theorems D.6, E.8, and F.6, absent from v2. Their development introduces regularized objectives, convexity and Hessian-smoothness assumptions, and proofs comparing influence updates with Newton approximations and retraining.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction contributions, and conclusion retain the same central claims: editable CBMs at three levels, influence-function approximations avoiding full retraining, and EK-FAC acceleration. The additional theory and experiments do not redefine those contributions.

C2.justification: New theoretical remarks interpret dependence on regularization and deletion counts. Remark D.8 explains why error bounds cover the concept predictor alone, discussing coupled inputs, error propagation, and inexpensive label-predictor retraining. Appendix H.2–H.3 also interprets the added experiments as evidence of robustness and repeated-edit capability.

D1.justification: Appendix H.1 newly explains CUB concept preprocessing through class-level majority voting. H.4.1 details ranking concepts by performance loss after individual removals using retraining or ECBM. These clarify retained experiments without establishing that their implementation changed.

R1.justification: Appendix I adds a substantial model-unlearning discussion distinguishing exact and approximate approaches, including Hessian, neural-tangent-kernel, and SGD-trajectory methods. New references include Bourtoule, Guo, Izzo, Mehta, Wu, and Thudi. The paper newly contrasts these approaches with CBM architecture and correction requirements.

P1.justification: V3 revises preliminaries and selected method explanations, introduces gradient shorthand, reorganizes appendix subsections, and moves the visualization discussion into Appendix H.4. It also updates the author information and adds impact and limitations sections. Most of the original narrative remains.

P2.justification: The main paper changes from one-column to two-column layout, redistributing tables and figures. V3 adds notation Table 2 and experimental Figures 5–8. V2 Figure 5 becomes appendix Figure 9, while the retained appendix visualizations are enlarged and redistributed across pages.

improvement.justification: The added noise-removal and repeated-edit studies address useful empirical questions, and the preprocessing disclosure improves reproducibility. However, the unexplained runtime replacements conflict with the retained 22–30% explanation. New Remarks E.9/F.7 describe deletion-count dependence as linear despite quadratic terms in their bounds, and the Hessian definitions are inconsistent. These benefits and unresolved scientific-reporting problems prevent a reliable net quality judgment.
